content.value_statement: Large projects slow down when independent tasks run one at a time. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code split safe work into parallel agents and merge results.
actual_capabilities: Identifies tasks that can run in parallel by checking file, data, and order dependencies.
Uses the Task tool pattern to assign independent work to separate agents.
Shows when tests, type checks, and lint checks can run before dependent build steps.
Provides reporting formats for completed parallel tasks and changed files.
Warns against shared-file edits, dependent work, and database migrations in parallel.
limitations: It relies on the agent to detect dependencies accurately before starting parallel work.
It does not provide executable scripts or a custom scheduler.
It cannot prevent merge conflicts if agents ignore shared-file boundaries.
It should not be used for tasks that require strict ordering.

use_cases.title: Parallel Project Review
use_cases.description: Analyze structure, dependencies, and quality in separate agents before merging a concise report.

use_cases.title: Independent Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Split unrelated components or pages across agents while avoiding shared file conflicts.

use_cases.title: Faster Quality Checks
use_cases.description: Run independent validation tasks together, then run dependent build steps after prerequisites pass.

prompt_templates.title: Find Parallel Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my request and tell me which parts can run in parallel. Do not start work until you list dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Project Concurrently
prompt_templates.prompt: Use separate agents to inspect structure, dependencies, and code quality. Merge the findings into one short action list.

prompt_templates.title: Build Independent Features
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the header, footer, and settings page in parallel only if they touch separate files. Report conflicts before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multi-Step Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a parallel workflow for analysis, implementation, and validation. Mark which steps must remain sequential and explain why.

output_examples.input: Analyze this repository and explain the main areas.
output: Starts separate agents for structure, dependencies, and code quality review.
Merges the findings into one project overview with clear follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Build a header, footer, and sidebar.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies independent components, assigns separate agents, and returns one consolidated implementation summary.
It groups independent checks first, then schedules build work after earlier checks succeed.

best_practices: List each task, expected files, and dependencies before starting agents.
Keep each parallel agent scoped to separate files or directories.
Merge results in one final report with failures and changed files.
anti_patterns: Do not parallelize tasks that edit the same file.
Do not parallelize database migrations or stateful deployment steps.
Do not launch agents before defining clear boundaries and acceptance checks.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps an agent divide independent work into parallel tasks and combine the results.

faq.question: Which tools does it use?
faq.answer: The skill declares Read and Task as allowed tools in its metadata.

faq.question: Does it execute commands by itself?
faq.answer: No. It describes workflow patterns and relies on tools available in the host environment.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when work has independent files, independent data, and no required execution order.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it for shared-file edits, dependent implementation steps, and database migrations.

faq.question: Can it help with code review?
faq.answer: Yes. It can split structure, dependency, and quality review across separate agents.
